resources.string: Space is an infinite, silent expanse that begins roughly 100 kilometers (62 miles) above Earth at the Kármán line. It is a near-perfect vacuum, completely devoid of matter and air, which means sound cannot travel through it. This vast void is punctuated by billions of galaxies, each containing hundreds of billions of stars, planets, and cosmic dust. Governed by the laws of physics and the warping of spacetime, it holds extreme environments—from the crushing gravity of black holes to the freezing remnants of the Big Bang. Driven by curiosity, humanity continues to explore this frontier, using advanced telescopes and spacecraft to peer into the past and unlock the mysteries of the universe.
